text:
inc-bot: PAGER: High-severity failover event for service:redwood-inference-api at 2026-05-05T09:17Z. Trigger: upstream transit provider reported partial blackholing of our us-east-1 egress prefixes; automated multi-region failover engaged to eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Severity P1. @oncall-marcus please ack.

oncall-marcus: ack  I'm looking at dashboards. NA customers seeing sudden 502/504 spike and stream reconnects. pulling recent deploys and routing changes.

prod-support-jordan: getting priority tickets from dataforge and streamly — both reporting session resets and prolonged reconnect loops. notifying account teams.

net-alyssa: provider shows large-scale withdraws for our transit AS on several IXes feeding us-east-1; return path asymmetry causing SYNs to reach region but responses never return for many client subnets. Anycast front-ends partly healthy but origin connectivity broken.

infra-wei: ALB/NGINX frontends in us-east-1 are intermittently failing health checks upstream; automated failover kicked in but it appears some target-groups in fallback regions still have long-lived backends registered -> sticky connections + duplicate request arrivals.

oncall-marcus: what's the autofailover id and drain state? don't want half-drained pools.

cloud-ops-bot: autofailover run id: AF-20260505-0917. Drain progress: 41%. DNS TTL at trigger: 75s. Canary: eu-west-1 12%.

pagerduty-bot: Notification: oncall-marcus paged via phone at 09:18Z.

net-alyssa: TTL=75s is high for this; edge caches will keep sending some traffic to the broken region. I'm setting TTL to 10s now and will trigger CDN invalidation for the api wildcard.

infra-wei: automation seems to have left a small set of legacy ASGs from a failed rolling deploy still registered; those instances have keepalives of 120s and are reintroducing stale connections. Recommend pause automation and do manual controlled reroute.

oncall-marcus: pause automation. @cloud-ops-bot pause AF-20260505-0917.

cloud-ops-bot: Command received from oncall-marcus. Pausing autofailover AF-20260505-0917... paused.

prod-support-jordan: sending interim customer message: "We're aware of connectivity problems for some regions. Engineering has initiated mitigation and is performing a controlled migration; we'll update in 15 minutes."

oncall-mei: suggestion: 1) set LB deregistration_delay to 3s for affected TGs, 2) reduce proxy keepalive to 10s, 3) clear connection pools in fallback regions, 4) apply small canary (5%) then ramp, 5) add short reconnect-rate-limit at edge (per-IP). Approve?

oncall-marcus: approve. start with canary and low dereg delay. We should also avoid flipping live IPs for whitelisted customers without notifying them.

infra-wei: executing commands now: 
```
# quick ALB tune
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn tg-redwood-api-use1 --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=3
# lower proxy keepalive
autoctl set proxy.keepalive --region eu-west-1 --value 10s
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/proxy --selector=region=eu-west-1
```
Applied to eu-west-1 first.

net-alyssa: DNS TTL lowered to 10s and CDN invalidation requested. Provider ticket SR-TRANSIT-5512 opened for transit blackholing. They acknowledge and are investigating configuration on their exchange routers.

cloud-ops-bot: Manual route change requested: canary eu-west-1 5% then ramp to 40% if healthy. Approve?

oncall-marcus: approve. start canary and watch 5xx and streaming handshakes.

cloud-ops-bot: Manual route applied: eu-west-1 canary 5% at 09:27Z.

prod-support-jordan: communicated canary to key customers; dataforge asked for fallback IPs for allowlist; sharing offline with security.

infra-wei: canary metrics: 5xx for canary 0.9% (baseline 0.3%), p95 latency slightly elevated. No reconnect storm at canary size. proceeding to ramp to 40% over 4m.

oncall-mei: ramp but keep a small 5% portion to us-west-2 as second fallback. Also enable short-term per-client reconnect limit at edge (8/s) in log-mode then enforce if required.

net-alyssa: ramp applied: eu-west-1 40% at 09:34Z; us-west-2 5% warm standby. Edge rate-limit rule deployed (log-mode).

prod-support-jordan: customer updates posted. Streamly reported fewer reconnects. Collecting session ids for detailed logs.

oncall-marcus: monitoring: global 5xx peaked 21% at 09:22Z, after mitigations down to 5.2% and trending down. Some long-lived websockets still need reconnects but overall success improving.

infra-wei: scaled eu-west-1 +30% and us-west-2 +25% to accept redirected QPS. Clearing pools post-scale.

net-alyssa: provider SR-TRANSIT-5512 update: "We've confirmed erroneous route filter applied at IX vendor for prefix set; reverting changes now. We'll provide ETA for full propagation ~40-60 minutes." They advise leaving manual routing until stable.

oncall-mei: agreed. keep manual route and don't flip back until transit confirms. mark incident as Mitigated (customer-facing impact reduced) but not Resolved.

prod-support-jordan: preparing post-incident customer synopsis: affected tenants: dataforge, streamly, and ~9 others; window ~09:17-09:40Z for most customers; impact: streaming disconnects and elevated 5xx; mitigation: manual routing, pool clears, DNS TTL change, edge invalidation; pending: transit provider confirmation, runbook updates for TTL automation.

cloud-ops-bot: Incident Mitigation Update  status: mitigated, incident id: INC-20260505-078. Postmortem scheduled 2026-05-06 14:00Z.

infra-wei: follow-ups: add a pre-check in failover automation to verify no active rolling deploys and to detect long-lived keepalive settings; add an automatic TTL reduction step when failover triggers. Filing JIRA: INFRA-7842.

oncall-marcus: handing off to oncall-mei at 10:00Z for extended watch until 22:00Z. Handoff notes posted to #eng-oncall. Escalation criteria: sustained 5xx >5% for 10m or streaming error rate >2% sustained.

oncall-mei: taking over. ack. I'll watch SR-TRANSIT-5512 and rollback plan.

prod-support-jordan: final customer update posted: "Service mitigated; controlled traffic shift in place and engineering is monitoring. We'll publish a detailed timeline and root cause once transit confirms full fix." Closing bridge. :white_check_mark:
